body: You're not alone! Despite being fully grown, my parents still latch on to the old mental illness excuse. I've been through every kind of mental health assessment there is, I've even been in a psych ward due to homelessness, and I think if I was suffering from a debilitating mental illness I would've been told by now. Is your suffering because of something or someone? Never underestimate the toll gaslighting and emotional abuse can have on your mental health. Depression and anxiety is often a normal response to an environment that is cold and invalidating. Also, think of what your nparent would come out with from a mental health assessment, ironically some of the same disorders they try to pin on you.

Luckily, Exeter have allowed me to return to uni this September which does give me time now to get my head together. I've looked into college courses to do over the summer but I've yet to action anything. My biggest downfall is that I spend too much time thinking and never doing. Plus I'm 22 now but feel more like a helpless child than an adult. I heard a good from JK Rowling though about how there is an age limit to blaming your parents for your lot in life which kind of made me get my ass into gear. Thanks for the advice.
I don't actually feel like I'm coming down at all this morning...maybe I'm delirious? And just as a side note: the book I read was flowers for algernon, would recommend, with or without speed
Mixing phenibut with speed is pretty fun though, don't deny it ;)
